name: Henbit

facts.how: Raw in salads or wilted like spinach
facts.when: The cool months, January to April
facts.where: Every winter lawn and fallow bed in Texas

caution: Unsprayed ground only; winter lawns are heavily treated. Henbit is not a true dead-nettle stinger and has no dangerous look-alike, but confirm the square stem and clasping scalloped leaves.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A mint-family winter annual: square stems, scalloped leaves clasping the stem in tiers, tiny orchid-like purple flowers. It carpets bare winter ground.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: Mild, slightly grassy, one of the first fresh greens of the year. Toss young tops raw, or wilt handfuls into eggs and soups.
